نَبَّاحٌ A dog that barks much. (A.) ―
-b2- نَبَّاحٌ A man (L) having a vehement, or loud, voice. (L, K.) ―
-b3- ↓ نُبَّاحٌ , with dammeh, (K,) or نَبَّاحٌ (as in the L) (tropical:) A hoopoe (هُدْهُد) that cooes (يُقَرْقِر) much. (IAar, K.) ―
-b4- نَبَّاحٌ (tropical:) A gazelle that cries much, or often: (IAar:) and ↓ نَبْحَآءُ the same applied to the female. (AA, K.) ＝
-A2- نَبَّاحٌ White, small [shells such as are called] صَدَف: (TA:) small, white [shells such as are called] مَنَاقِف, of Mekkeh, (T, K, TA,) i. e. brought from Mekkeh: (TA:) put into [necklaces such as are called] قَلَائِد (K, TA) and وُشُح, and used for repelling the [evil] eye: (TA:) n. un. with ة. (K.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
